# Coder Infrastructure Changes

## Overview

This specification defines the changes needed to the `coder-infra` repository to support the sudopod Coder provider. The changes include:

1. **OIDC Configuration** - Enable Google OIDC for sudocode-hub authentication
2. **Template Updates** - Enhance the `sudocode-workspace` template for sudopod integration
3. **Agent Installation** - Support for installing AI agents (Claude, etc.)

## Repository

All changes are made to: `github.com/sudocodeai/coder-infra`

## 1. OIDC Configuration

### docker-compose.yml Changes

Add OIDC environment variables to support Google authentication for sudocode-hub:

```yaml
services:
  coder:
    image: ghcr.io/coder/coder:v2.8.0
    environment:
      # ... existing config ...
      
      # OIDC Configuration (for sudocode-hub integration)
      # These can be overridden via .env file for different environments
      - CODER_OIDC_ISSUER_URL=${CODER_OIDC_ISSUER_URL:-}
      - CODER_OIDC_CLIENT_ID=${CODER_OIDC_CLIENT_ID:-}
      - CODER_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=${CODER_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET:-}
      - CODER_OIDC_EMAIL_DOMAIN=${CODER_OIDC_EMAIL_DOMAIN:-*}
      - CODER_OIDC_SCOPES=${CODER_OIDC_SCOPES:-openid,profile,email}
      - CODER_OIDC_SIGN_IN_TEXT=${CODER_OIDC_SIGN_IN_TEXT:-Sign in with Google}
      - CODER_OIDC_ICON_URL=${CODER_OIDC_ICON_URL:-/icon/google.svg}
      - CODER_OIDC_AUTH_URL_PARAMS=${CODER_OIDC_AUTH_URL_PARAMS:-{"access_type": "offline", "prompt": "consent"}}
      - CODER_OIDC_ALLOW_SIGNUPS=${CODER_OIDC_ALLOW_SIGNUPS:-true}
```

### .env.example File

Create `.env.example` for OIDC configuration:

```bash
# Coder OIDC Configuration
# Copy to .env and fill in your values

# Google OAuth (get from Google Cloud Console)
CODER_OIDC_ISSUER_URL=https://accounts.google.com
CODER_OIDC_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id.apps.googleusercontent.com
CODER_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret

# Restrict to specific domain (use * for any domain)
CODER_OIDC_EMAIL_DOMAIN=*

# UI customization
CODER_OIDC_SIGN_IN_TEXT=Sign in with Google
CODER_OIDC_ICON_URL=/icon/google.svg
```

### Local Testing Setup

Add `docs/oidc-setup.md`:

```markdown
# Setting up OIDC for Local Development

## 1. Create Google OAuth Credentials

1. Go to [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com)
2. APIs & Services → Credentials → Create Credentials → OAuth client ID
3. Application type: Web application
4. Authorized redirect URIs: `http://localhost:7080/api/v2/users/oidc/callback`
5. Save Client ID and Client Secret

## 2. Configure Coder

Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill in your credentials:

```bash
cp .env.example .env
# Edit .env with your Google OAuth credentials
```

## 3. Start Coder

```bash
docker compose up
```

## 4. Test OIDC Login

1. Go to http://localhost:7080
2. Click "Sign in with Google"
3. Login with your Google account
4. You should see the Coder dashboard
```

## 2. Template Updates

### Updated main.tf

Location: `templates/sudocode-workspace/main.tf`

```hcl
terraform {
  required_providers {
    coder = {
      source  = "coder/coder"
      version = "~> 0.12"
    }
    docker = {
      source  = "kreuzwerker/docker"
      version = "~> 3.0"
    }
  }
}

provider "docker" {
  host = "unix:///var/run/docker.sock"
}

# ============================================================================
# PARAMETERS
# ============================================================================

data "coder_parameter" "repository" {
  name         = "repository"
  display_name = "Repository URL"
  description  = "Git repository to clone (HTTPS URL)"
  type         = "string"
  mutable      = false
  order        = 1
}

data "coder_parameter" "branch" {
  name         = "branch"
  display_name = "Branch"
  description  = "Git branch to checkout"
  type         = "string"
  default      = "main"
  mutable      = true
  order        = 2
}

data "coder_parameter" "github_token" {
  name         = "github_token"
  display_name = "GitHub Token"
  description  = "GitHub token for cloning private repositories"
  type         = "string"
  default      = ""
  mutable      = true
  order        = 3
  # Note: Coder parameters are stored securely
}

data "coder_parameter" "agents" {
  name         = "agents"
  display_name = "AI Agents"
  description  = "Comma-separated list of agents to install (e.g., 'claude')"
  type         = "string"
  default      = "claude"
  mutable      = true
  order        = 4
}

variable "sudocode_version" {
  description = "sudocode version (npm version or 'latest')"
  type        = string
  default     = "latest"
}

variable "machine_type" {
  description = "Machine type: small, medium, or large"
  type        = string
  default     = "small"
  
  validation {
    condition     = contains(["small", "medium", "large"], var.machine_type)
    error_message = "machine_type must be small, medium, or large"
  }
}

variable "memory_gb" {
  description = "Memory in GB (6-32)"
  type        = number
  default     = 8
  
  validation {
    condition     = var.memory_gb >= 6 && var.memory_gb <= 32
    error_message = "memory_gb must be between 6 and 32"
  }
}

variable "storage_gb" {
  description = "Storage in GB"
  type        = number
  default     = 50
  
  validation {
    condition     = var.storage_gb >= 30
    error_message = "storage_gb must be at least 30"
  }
}

variable "idle_timeout_minutes" {
  description = "Minutes before auto-stop"
  type        = number
  default     = 60
}

variable "max_ttl_hours" {
  description = "Hours before workspace deletion"
  type        = number
  default     = 168
}

variable "docker_network" {
  description = "Docker network name for workspace containers"
  type        = string
  default     = "coder-network"
}

variable "user_secrets" {
  description = "User-defined secrets as JSON string"
  type        = string
  default     = "{}"
  sensitive   = true
}

# ============================================================================
# LOCALS
# ============================================================================

locals {
  cpu_cores = {
    small  = 4
    medium = 8
    large  = 16
  }
  
  workspace_cpu = local.cpu_cores[var.machine_type]
  
  # Parse agents list
  agents_list = split(",", trimspace(data.coder_parameter.agents.value))
  
  # Parse user secrets
  secrets = jsondecode(var.user_secrets)
}

# ============================================================================
# DATA SOURCES
# ============================================================================

data "coder_workspace" "me" {}
data "coder_workspace_owner" "me" {}

# ============================================================================
# PERSISTENT VOLUMES
# ============================================================================

resource "docker_volume" "workspace" {
  name = "coder-${data.coder_workspace_owner.me.name}-${data.coder_workspace.me.name}-workspace"
  
  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = all
  }
}

resource "docker_volume" "sudocode" {
  name = "coder-${data.coder_workspace_owner.me.name}-${data.coder_workspace.me.name}-sudocode"
  
  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = all
  }
}

# ============================================================================
# AGENT & APPS
# ============================================================================

resource "coder_agent" "main" {
  os   = "linux"
  arch = "amd64"
  
  env = {
    REPOSITORY       = data.coder_parameter.repository.value
    BRANCH           = data.coder_parameter.branch.value
    GITHUB_TOKEN     = data.coder_parameter.github_token.value
    SUDOCODE_VERSION = var.sudocode_version
    AGENTS           = data.coder_parameter.agents.value
  }
  
  metadata {
    display_name = "CPU Usage"
    key          = "cpu"
    script       = "coder stat cpu"
    interval     = 10
    timeout      = 1
  }
  
  metadata {
    display_name = "Memory Usage"
    key          = "mem"
    script       = "coder stat mem"
    interval     = 10
    timeout      = 1
  }
  
  metadata {
    display_name = "Disk Usage"
    key          = "disk"
    script       = "df -h /workspace | awk 'NR==2 {print $5}'"
    interval     = 60
    timeout      = 1
  }
}

# Startup script runs on every workspace start
resource "coder_script" "startup" {
  agent_id     = coder_agent.main.id
  display_name = "Workspace Setup"
  icon         = "/icon/coder.svg"
  run_on_start = true
  
  script = file("${path.module}/startup.sh")
}

resource "coder_app" "vscode" {
  agent_id     = coder_agent.main.id
  slug         = "vscode"
  display_name = "VS Code"
  url          = "http://localhost:8080"
  icon         = "/icon/code.svg"
  subdomain    = true
  share        = "owner"
}

resource "coder_app" "sudocode" {
  agent_id     = coder_agent.main.id
  slug         = "sudocode"
  display_name = "sudocode"
  url          = "http://localhost:3000"
  icon         = "/icon/terminal.svg"
  subdomain    = true
  share        = "owner"
}

# ============================================================================
# DOCKER CONTAINER
# ============================================================================

resource "docker_image" "workspace" {
  name = "codercom/enterprise-base:ubuntu"
}

resource "docker_container" "workspace" {
  count = data.coder_workspace.me.start_count
  
  image = docker_image.workspace.name
  name  = "coder-${data.coder_workspace_owner.me.name}-${data.coder_workspace.me.name}"
  
  cpu_shares = local.workspace_cpu * 1024
  memory     = var.memory_gb * 1024 * 1024 * 1024
  
  networks_advanced {
    name = var.docker_network
  }
  
  volumes {
    container_path = "/workspace"
    volume_name    = docker_volume.workspace.name
  }
  
  volumes {
    container_path = "/sudocode"
    volume_name    = docker_volume.sudocode.name
  }
  
  env = [
    "CODER_AGENT_TOKEN=${coder_agent.main.token}",
  ]
  
  host {
    host = "host.docker.internal"
    ip   = "host-gateway"
  }
  
  command = ["sh", "-c", coder_agent.main.init_script]
}
```

### Updated startup.sh

Location: `templates/sudocode-workspace/startup.sh`

```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -e

LOG_DIR="/sudocode/logs"
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"

log() {
  echo "[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] $1" | tee -a "$LOG_DIR/startup.log"
}

log "🚀 Initializing sudocode workspace..."

# ============================================================================
# STEP 1: Clone or update repository (cold vs warm start)
# ============================================================================

REPO_NAME=$(basename "$REPOSITORY" .git)
WORKSPACE_DIR="/workspace/$REPO_NAME"

if [ -d "$WORKSPACE_DIR/.git" ]; then
  log "Warm start: repo exists, pulling latest..."
  cd "$WORKSPACE_DIR"
  
  # Use GitHub token if provided
  if [ -n "$GITHUB_TOKEN" ]; then
    git remote set-url origin "https://x-access-token:${GITHUB_TOKEN}@${REPOSITORY#https://}"
  fi
  
  git fetch origin
  git checkout "${BRANCH:-main}"
  git pull origin "${BRANCH:-main}" || log "⚠️ Pull failed, continuing with existing code"
else
  log "Cold start: cloning repo..."
  mkdir -p "/workspace"
  
  if [ -n "$GITHUB_TOKEN" ]; then
    git clone --branch "${BRANCH:-main}" "https://x-access-token:${GITHUB_TOKEN}@${REPOSITORY#https://}" "$WORKSPACE_DIR"
  else
    git clone --branch "${BRANCH:-main}" "$REPOSITORY" "$WORKSPACE_DIR"
  fi
fi

cd "$WORKSPACE_DIR"

# ============================================================================
# STEP 2: Install system dependencies
# ============================================================================

log "Installing system dependencies..."
if ! dpkg -l | grep -q build-essential; then
  sudo apt-get update
  sudo apt-get install -y git curl wget build-essential
fi

# Install Node.js 20.x if not present
if ! command -v node &> /dev/null; then
  log "Installing Node.js 20.x..."
  curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_20.x | sudo -E bash -
  sudo apt-get install -y nodejs
fi

# ============================================================================
# STEP 3: Handle devcontainer
# ============================================================================

DEVCONTAINER_PATH="$WORKSPACE_DIR/.devcontainer/devcontainer.json"

if [ -f "$DEVCONTAINER_PATH" ]; then
  log "✅ Found devcontainer.json in repository"
  
  if ! command -v devcontainer &> /dev/null; then
    log "Installing @devcontainers/cli..."
    sudo npm install -g @devcontainers/cli
  fi
  
  # Note: In Docker-in-Docker setup, we run devcontainer inside the workspace
  # For now, we just validate the devcontainer exists
  log "Devcontainer configuration detected (build handled separately)"
else
  log "⚠️ No devcontainer.json found, using workspace directly"
fi

# ============================================================================
# STEP 4: Install sudocode
# ============================================================================

log "Installing sudocode ($SUDOCODE_VERSION)..."

if [ "$SUDOCODE_VERSION" = "latest" ]; then
  sudo npm install -g sudocode
else
  sudo npm install -g "sudocode@$SUDOCODE_VERSION"
fi

log "✅ sudocode installed: $(sudocode --version 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"

# ============================================================================
# STEP 5: Install AI agents
# ============================================================================

log "Installing agents: $AGENTS"

IFS=',' read -ra AGENT_ARRAY <<< "$AGENTS"
for agent in "${AGENT_ARRAY[@]}"; do
  agent=$(echo "$agent" | xargs)  # trim whitespace
  
  case "$agent" in
    claude)
      if ! command -v claude &> /dev/null; then
        log "Installing Claude..."
        curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash
        log "✅ Claude installed"
      else
        log "Claude already installed"
      fi
      ;;
    *)
      log "⚠️ Unknown agent: $agent, skipping..."
      ;;
  esac
done

# ============================================================================
# STEP 6: Install VS Code Server
# ============================================================================

if ! command -v code-server &> /dev/null; then
  log "Installing VS Code Server..."
  curl -fsSL https://code-server.dev/install.sh | sh
fi

# ============================================================================
# STEP 7: Create systemd services
# ============================================================================

log "Creating systemd services..."

# sudocode service
sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/sudocode.service > /dev/null <<EOF
[Unit]
Description=sudocode Server
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=coder
WorkingDirectory=$WORKSPACE_DIR
ExecStart=/usr/bin/npx sudocode start --port 3000
Restart=always
RestartSec=10
StandardOutput=append:$LOG_DIR/server.log
StandardError=append:$LOG_DIR/server.log

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF

# code-server service
sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/code-server.service > /dev/null <<EOF
[Unit]
Description=VS Code Server
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=coder
WorkingDirectory=$WORKSPACE_DIR
ExecStart=/usr/bin/code-server --bind-addr 0.0.0.0:8080 --auth none $WORKSPACE_DIR
Restart=always
RestartSec=10
StandardOutput=journal
StandardError=journal

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF

sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable sudocode code-server
sudo systemctl start sudocode code-server

# ============================================================================
# DONE
# ============================================================================

log "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
log "✅ Workspace initialized successfully!"
log "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
log "📍 Repository: $WORKSPACE_DIR"
log "🌿 Branch: ${BRANCH:-main}"
log "🤖 Agents: $AGENTS"
log ""
log "🌐 Services:"
log "  - VS Code:    http://localhost:8080"
log "  - sudocode:   http://localhost:3000"
log ""
log "📋 Logs: $LOG_DIR/"
log "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
```

title: Authentication Architecture: OIDC + GitHub App
content:
# Authentication Architecture: OIDC + GitHub App

## Overview

This specification defines user authentication for sudocode deployments. The architecture separates **authentication** (identity) from **authorization** (repo access):

- **Authentication**: Google OIDC (or enterprise IdP like Okta)
- **Authorization**: GitHub App for repository access

## Key Design Decision: Separation of Concerns

### Why Not Shared GitHub OAuth?

The original plan was to share a GitHub OAuth app between hub and Coder. Investigation revealed this is **not viable**:

- **GitHub OAuth Apps** only support a single callback URL (host+port must match)
- **GitHub Apps** support multiple callback URLs, but Coder only supports OAuth Apps for authentication
- See [[i-41sx]] for detailed findings

### The Solution: OIDC for Auth, GitHub App for Repos

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ AUTHENTICATION (Identity)                                           │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Both Hub and Coder use the same OIDC provider:                     │
│  - Default: Google OIDC (free, widely available)                    │
│  - Enterprise: Customer's Okta/Azure AD                             │
│                                                                     │
│  User signs in once → same identity across both systems             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ AUTHORIZATION (Repo Access)                                         │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  GitHub App (separate from authentication):                         │
│  - User connects GitHub account on hub                              │
│  - Grants access to specific repositories                           │
│  - Token stored and used for git operations in workspaces           │
│                                                                     │
│  This is NOT used for login - only for repo access                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## User Flow

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1. USER SIGNS UP ON SUDOCODE-HUB                                    │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  User clicks "Sign in with Google" on hub                           │
│  → Google OIDC consent screen                                       │
│  → Hub receives id_token, extracts email                            │
│  → User account created in hub                                      │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                  │
                                  ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 2. USER CONNECTS GITHUB (Separate Step)                             │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  User clicks "Connect GitHub" in hub settings                       │
│  → GitHub App authorization screen                                  │
│  → User selects repositories to grant access                        │
│  → Hub stores GitHub token for repo operations                      │
│                                                                     │
│  NOTE: This is authorization, not authentication                    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                  │
                                  ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 3. HUB PROVISIONS USER IN CODER (via API)                           │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  POST /api/v2/users                                                 │
│  {                                                                  │
│    "username": "developer",                                         │
│    "email": "developer@gmail.com",  ← Google email                  │
│    "login_type": "oidc",                                            │
│    "organization_ids": ["org-uuid"]                                 │
│  }                                                                  │
│                                                                     │
│  User created with status: "dormant"                                │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                  │
                                  ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 4. HUB CREATES WORKSPACE FOR USER (via API)                         │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  POST /api/v2/organizations/{org}/members/{user}/workspaces         │
│  {                                                                  │
│    "name": "dev",                                                   │
│    "template_id": "template-uuid"                                   │
│  }                                                                  │
│                                                                     │
│  Workspace created and running, waiting for user                    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                  │
                                  ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 5. USER ACCESSES CODER                                              │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  User clicks "Open Workspace" in hub                                │
│  → Redirects to Coder login                                         │
│  → User clicks "Sign in with Google"                                │
│  → Same Google account → NO NEW CONSENT (already authorized)        │
│  → Coder receives id_token, extracts email                          │
│  → Email matches pre-created user → Login successful                │
│  → User sees their pre-created workspace                            │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Controlled Access Model

Users cannot self-signup or create their own workspaces. Coder is configured with:

```bash
# Users must be pre-created via API (no auto-signup on first login)
CODER_OIDC_ALLOW_SIGNUPS=false

# OIDC configuration (Google)
CODER_OIDC_ISSUER_URL=https://accounts.google.com
CODER_OIDC_CLIENT_ID="..."
CODER_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET="..."
CODER_OIDC_EMAIL_DOMAIN="*"  # Allow any email domain
```

This means:
- ✅ Users pre-created by hub can log in via Google OIDC
- ❌ Random users cannot create accounts by logging in
- ❌ Users cannot create their own workspaces (only access pre-created ones)

## Authentication Modes

### Default: Google OIDC

Google is a full OIDC provider with:
- `https://accounts.google.com/.well-known/openid-configuration`
- Proper `id_token` issuance
- Free for authentication
- Widely available (most developers have Google accounts)

### Enterprise: Customer's IdP

For enterprises, Coder connects to their existing identity provider:

```bash
# Okta example
CODER_OIDC_ISSUER_URL="https://company.okta.com"
CODER_OIDC_CLIENT_ID="..."
CODER_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET="..."
CODER_OIDC_EMAIL_DOMAIN="company.com"
```

Hub would also need to support the same IdP, or enterprises manage user provisioning separately.

## Infrastructure Files

Implementation artifacts in `refs/coder-infra/`:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `docker-compose.oidc.yml` | Docker compose for OIDC mode (Google) |
| `.env.oidc.example` | Example environment configuration |
| `scripts/start-oidc-mode.sh` | Helper script for OIDC mode |
| `docs/oidc-setup-guide.md` | Setup documentation |

## Experiment Results

### Validated

| Test | Result | Issue | Notes |

| Template push via CLI | ✅ | [[i-3167]] | Session token auth works |

### Invalidated ([[i-41sx]])

## Implementation in Coder Primitives Library

The `ensureUser()` method should use OIDC login type:

```typescript

  username: string;
  email: string;
  loginType: 'oidc';  // OIDC is the standard

}

async ensureUser(options: EnsureUserOptions): Promise<User> {

```

## Decision Matrix: Which Auth to Use

| Customer Scenario | Auth Method | Notes |
|-------------------|-------------|-------|
| Default (sudocode.ai) | Google OIDC | Free, widely available |
| Enterprise with Okta | Okta OIDC | Direct integration |
| Enterprise with Azure AD | Azure AD OIDC | Direct integration |
| Enterprise with other IdP | Customer's OIDC | Custom config |

# Sudopod Provider Architecture

## Overview

This specification defines the architecture for sudopod providers - the system that enables sudocode to create and manage remote development workspaces across different infrastructure backends.

**Supersedes:** [[s-eley]] (Coder Provider Architecture and Implementation)

## Terminology

- **Provider**: The host-side implementation that actually provisions workspaces (e.g., CoderProvider). Implements the `Provider` interface and runs in infrastructure repos like coder-infra.
- **Connector**: The CLI-side adapter that routes requests to providers (e.g., HubConnector, SelfHostedConnector, CodespacesConnector). Used by the sudocode CLI.

## Three Deployment Models

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    MODEL 1: DIRECT CONNECTOR                        │
│                    (Codespaces)                                     │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                     │
│  [sudocode CLI] ──► [sudopod library] ──► [External API]            │
│                     CodespacesConnector    (GitHub-hosted)          │
│                                                                     │
│  • No infrastructure to manage                                      │
│  • Connector talks directly to external API                         │
│  • Auth via user's existing credentials (gh CLI)                    │
│                                                                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    MODEL 2: HUB-MANAGED PROVIDER                    │
│                    (sudocode-hub hosted Coder)                      │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                     │
│  [sudocode CLI] ──► [sudopod] ──► [sudocode-hub] ──► [Provider Host]│
│                     HubConnector   (injects secrets)   (coder-infra)│
│                                                                     │
│  CLI provides:  repository, branch, resources                       │
│  Hub injects:   githubToken, secrets, userIdentity                  │
│  Hub routes to: Provider host URL with API key auth                 │
│                                                                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    MODEL 3: SELF-HOSTED PROVIDER                    │
│                    (User's own coder-infra deployment)              │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                     │
│  [sudocode CLI] ──► [sudopod] ──► [User's Provider Host]            │
│                     SelfHostedConnector                             │
│                                                                     │
│  CLI provides:    repository, branch, resources                     │
│  Config provides: providerUrl, apiKey, githubToken, secrets         │
│                                                                     │
│  User manages their own:                                            │
│  • Provider host URL (their coder-infra deployment)                 │
│  • API key for auth                                                 │
│  • GitHub token (from gh CLI or config)                             │
│  • Secrets (from local config)                                      │
│                                                                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Key Principles

1. **Hub is provider-agnostic**: sudocode-hub knows nothing about Coder, Kubernetes, etc. It only:
   - Routes to the correct provider host URL
   - Injects user's secrets and GitHub tokens
   - Passes user's identity (for OIDC)

2. **Translation lives in provider**: Each provider host (e.g., coder-infra) contains:
   - Standardized API server (from sudopod)
   - Provider-specific client (e.g., CoderClient)
   - Infrastructure sidecar (e.g., Coder server)

3. **Self-hosted mirrors hub**: SelfHostedConnector sends the same request format as hub would, but gets values from local config instead of hub injection.

4. **Shared client library**: Both hub and SelfHostedConnector use the same `SudopodClient` to call provider hosts.

## Repository Topology

```
sudopod/                          ◄── This repo
  src/types/                      ← Provider interface & request/response types
  src/server/                     ← Generic API server (for provider hosts)
  src/client/                     ← Client library (for hub & SelfHostedConnector)
  src/connectors/
    codespaces/                   ← Direct connector (GitHub API)
    hub/                          ← HubConnector (routes through hub)
    self-hosted/                  ← SelfHostedConnector (direct to provider host)

sudocode-hub/                     ◄── Separate repo
  imports: sudopod/client         ← Uses sudopod's client library
  imports: sudopod/types          ← Uses standardized types
  # Hub has NO provider-specific code

coder-infra/                      ◄── Separate repo
  imports: sudopod/server         ← Uses sudopod's generic server
  imports: sudopod/types          ← Implements Provider interface
  src/client/                     ← CoderClient (Coder-specific translation)
  src/provider/                   ← CoderProvider implementation
  docker-compose.yml              ← sudopod-server + Coder sidecar
  templates/                      ← Workspace templates

[future-provider]-infra/          ◄── Same pattern for other providers
  imports: sudopod/server
  imports: sudopod/types
  src/client/                     ← Provider-specific client
  src/provider/                   ← Provider implementation
  deployment/                     ← Infrastructure config
```

## sudopod Package Exports

```typescript
// sudopod/src/index.ts

// === For CLI consumers (connectors) ===
export { CodespacesConnector } from './connectors/codespaces';
export { HubConnector } from './connectors/hub';
export { SelfHostedConnector } from './connectors/self-hosted';
export { createConnector } from './factory';

// === For provider host implementations (coder-infra, etc.) ===
export { createServer } from './server';
export type { Provider, CreateWorkspaceRequest, Workspace } from './types';

// === For hub and SelfHostedConnector ===
export { SudopodClient } from './client';
```

## Sub-Specifications

This is a high-level architecture document. Detailed specifications for each component:

### Core Components (sudopod repo)

| Spec | Description |
|------|-------------|
| [[s-7gqg]] | **Provider Interface Contract** - The `Provider` TypeScript interface, request/response types (`CreateWorkspaceRequest`, `Workspace`, `UserIdentity`), and error types that all provider implementations must use. |
| [[s-2aqt]] | **Sudopod Server Implementation** - The `createServer()` function that wraps any Provider and exposes it as HTTP REST endpoints with API key authentication, request validation, and error handling. |

### Coder Provider (coder-infra repo)

| Spec | Description |
|------|-------------|
| [[s-5lwn]] | **CoderProvider Implementation** - The `CoderProvider` class that implements the `Provider` interface, translating standardized requests to Coder API calls. |
| [[s-7rdw]] | **Coder Provider Local Development** - Quick local setup with Docker compose for development and testing. |
| [[s-4xlf]] | **Coder Provider Production Deployment** - Production deployment with TLS, OIDC, monitoring, and operational procedures. |

### Related Specifications

| Spec | Description |
|------|-------------|
| [[s-9pwi]] | **Coder Primitives Library** - CoderClient implementation for low-level Coder API operations. |
| [[s-3h3r]] | **Authentication Architecture** - OIDC + GitHub App authentication flows. |
| [[s-8qk0]] | **Coder Infrastructure Changes** - Template and infrastructure configuration. |

## Client Library

The `SudopodClient` class provides a typed HTTP client for calling provider hosts. Used by:
- **sudocode-hub**: Routes requests to provider hosts, injecting user secrets and identity
- **SelfHostedConnector**: Calls provider hosts directly with user-provided config

Key methods: `createWorkspace()`, `getWorkspace()`, `deleteWorkspace()`, `listWorkspaces()`, `startWorkspace()`, `stopWorkspace()`

All methods use Bearer token authentication and return standardized types from [[s-7gqg]].

## Connector Overview

### CodespacesConnector
Direct connector that talks to GitHub's Codespaces API. Uses `gh` CLI for authentication. No sudopod server required.

### HubConnector
Routes requests through sudocode-hub:
- CLI provides: repository, branch, resources
- Hub injects: githubToken, secrets, userIdentity
- Hub routes to provider host with API key auth

### SelfHostedConnector
Calls provider hosts directly:
- Uses `SudopodClient` to communicate with provider
- Resolves GitHub token from config or `gh` CLI
- Includes secrets and userIdentity from local config

## Connector Configurations

```typescript
type ConnectorConfig = 
  | CodespacesConnectorConfig   // Uses gh CLI, no additional config
  | HubConnectorConfig          // hubUrl, hubToken, provider
  | SelfHostedConnectorConfig;  // providerUrl, apiKey, githubToken, secrets, userIdentity
```

## CLI Configuration

```yaml
# ~/.config/sudocode/connectors.yaml

# Option 1: Use Codespaces directly
default: codespaces
connectors:
  codespaces:
    type: codespaces

# Option 2: Use hub-managed Coder
default: hub-coder
connectors:
  hub-coder:
    type: hub
    hubUrl: https://hub.sudocode.ai
    hubToken: ${SUDOCODE_HUB_TOKEN}
    provider: coder

# Option 3: Self-hosted Coder
default: my-coder
connectors:
  my-coder:
    type: self-hosted
    providerUrl: https://coder.mycompany.com:8080
    apiKey: ${CODER_API_KEY}
    githubToken: gh-cli
    secrets:
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}
    userIdentity:
      email: me@company.com
```

## Comparison Summary

| Aspect | Codespaces | Hub | Self-Hosted |
|--------|------------|-----|-------------|
| Connector | CodespacesConnector | HubConnector | SelfHostedConnector |
| Auth to provider | gh CLI | Hub token → Hub → API key | API key directly |
| GitHub token | gh CLI | Hub (GitHub App) | Config or gh CLI |
| Secrets | N/A | Hub (user's stored secrets) | Local config |
| User identity | N/A | Hub (OAuth session) | Config (optional) |
| Infrastructure | GitHub-managed | sudocode-managed | User-managed |
| Provider host | N/A | hub.sudocode.ai routes | User's URL |

## Validation Requirements

### Critical E2E Test: Programmatic Create → Human Login

The most important validation for hub and self-hosted modes:

```
Test Flow:
1. API call creates user (OIDC) + workspace
2. User opens browser → Provider UI (e.g., Coder at https://coder.example.com)
3. User clicks "Sign in with Google"
4. User authenticates with same email used in step 1
5. User sees their workspace in the dashboard
6. User can connect to workspace (terminal, VS Code, etc.)
```

## Implementation Status

### Completed

- **Provider Interface & Types** ([[s-7gqg]]): Implemented
- **Sudopod Server** ([[s-2aqt]]): Implemented
- **CoderClient primitives** ([[s-9pwi]]): User and workspace management, 41 tests passing
- **OIDC authentication flow** ([[s-3h3r]]): Validated end-to-end

### Remaining Work

1. **sudopod Client Library** - Implement `SudopodClient` in `src/client/`
2. **sudopod Connectors** - HubConnector and SelfHostedConnector
3. **coder-infra** - CoderProvider using sudopod Provider interface
4. **E2E Validation** - Script for programmatic create → human login test

## Decision Log

### Provider vs Connector Terminology (2026-01-24)

Clarified naming to distinguish two concepts:
- **Provider**: Host-side implementation that provisions workspaces (CoderProvider, etc.). Implements the `Provider` interface.
- **Connector**: CLI-side adapter that routes to providers (HubConnector, SelfHostedConnector, CodespacesConnector).

### Hub as Pure Proxy (2026-01-23)

Decided that sudocode-hub should have zero provider-specific logic. The translation layer lives entirely in each provider's infrastructure repo. Hub only handles:
- Routing to correct provider host
- Injecting user secrets and GitHub tokens
- Passing user identity for OIDC

### CoderClient Location (2026-01-23)

Decided CoderClient should live in coder-infra, not sudopod. Rationale:
- sudopod stays clean as a library + generic server + client
- Each provider repo is self-contained
- No Coder-specific code in the shared library

### Self-Hosted Model (2026-01-23)

Added self-hosted connector model where users can:
- Deploy their own coder-infra (or any provider-infra)
- Configure CLI to point to their provider host URL
- Provide their own API key, GitHub token, and secrets
- Optionally provide userEmail for OIDC user creation

### Shared Client Library (2026-01-23)

Both hub and SelfHostedConnector use the same `SudopodClient` class to call provider hosts. This ensures:
- Consistent request/response handling
- Single place to implement retries, error handling
- Hub and self-hosted are functionally equivalent

### User Identity vs Email (2026-01-24)

Changed from `userEmail: string` to `userIdentity` object with optional OIDC claims:
- `email` - Primary identifier for OIDC user matching
- `sub` - OIDC subject identifier (IdP's internal user ID)
- `username` - Preferred username

### Provider Server Admin Bootstrap (2026-01-24)

The provider server (e.g., coder-infra) handles its own initialization:
1. On first startup, creates admin user via `/api/v2/users/first` (no auth required)
2. Logs in to get session token
3. Creates long-lived API token (~100 year lifetime in Coder)
4. Persists credentials to `/var/lib/sudopod/coder-credentials.json`

# Coder Provider Local Development

## Overview

This specification defines how to run the CoderProvider locally for development and testing. The focus is on quick setup, validating the CoderProvider works, and running integration tests.

**Parent:** [[s-1u2m]] (Sudopod Provider Architecture)
**Implements:** [[s-5lwn]] (CoderProvider Implementation)
**Production deployment:** [[s-TODO]] (Coder Provider Production Deployment)

## Goals

- Get CoderProvider running locally in < 5 minutes
- No OIDC setup required (uses password auth for testing)
- Validate workspace creation/deletion via API
- Support integration test suite

## Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                  Local Development Stack                         │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                  │
│  ┌──────────────────┐         ┌──────────────────┐              │
│  │   sudopod-api    │────────▶│     coder        │              │
│  │   (port 8080)    │         │   (port 7080)    │              │
│  │                  │         │                  │              │
│  │  - CoderProvider │         │  - Coder server  │              │
│  │  - HTTP server   │         │  - Password auth │              │
│  │  - API key auth  │         │  - Workspace mgmt│              │
│  └──────────────────┘         └──────────────────┘              │
│           │                            │                         │
│           ▼                            ▼                         │
│  ┌──────────────────┐         ┌──────────────────┐              │
│  │   credentials    │         │    postgres      │              │
│  │   (volume)       │         │   (port 5432)    │              │
│  └──────────────────┘         └──────────────────┘              │
│                                                                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Quick Start

### Prerequisites

- Docker and Docker Compose
- Node.js 20+ (for local development without Docker)
- ~4GB free memory

### 1. Clone and Setup

```bash
git clone https://github.com/sudocodeai/coder-infra
cd coder-infra

# Copy example env (uses sensible defaults for local dev)
cp .env.example .env.local
```

### 2. Start Services

```bash
# Start everything
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.local.yml up -d

# Watch logs
docker compose logs -f
```

### 3. Verify

```bash
# Check health
curl http://localhost:8080/health

# Create a test workspace
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/workspaces \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer dev-api-key" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "repository": "octocat/Hello-World",
    "userIdentity": {"email": "test@example.com"}
  }'
```

## Docker Compose Configuration

### Base Configuration

```yaml
# coder-infra/docker-compose.yml

version: '3.8'

services:
  sudopod-api:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    ports:
      - "${SUDOPOD_PORT:-8080}:8080"
    environment:
      - CODER_URL=http://coder:7080
      - CODER_TEMPLATE=${CODER_TEMPLATE:-sudocode-workspace}
      - SUDOPOD_API_KEYS=${SUDOPOD_API_KEYS:-dev-api-key}
      - CODER_ADMIN_EMAIL=${CODER_ADMIN_EMAIL:-admin@sudocode.local}
    volumes:
      - sudopod-credentials:/var/lib/sudopod
    depends_on:
      coder:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:8080/health"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  coder:
    image: ghcr.io/coder/coder:${CODER_VERSION:-latest}
    ports:
      - "${CODER_PORT:-7080}:7080"
    environment:
      - CODER_ACCESS_URL=${CODER_ACCESS_URL:-http://localhost:7080}
      - CODER_HTTP_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0:7080
      - CODER_PG_CONNECTION_URL=postgresql://coder:coder@postgres:5432/coder?sslmode=disable
      - CODER_TELEMETRY_ENABLE=false
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - coder-data:/var/lib/coder
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:7080/api/v2/buildinfo"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 60s

  postgres:
    image: postgres:15-alpine
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_USER=coder
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=coder
      - POSTGRES_DB=coder
    volumes:
      - postgres-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U coder -d coder"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

volumes:
  sudopod-credentials:
  coder-data:
  postgres-data:

networks:
  default:
    name: coder-network
```

### Local Development Overrides

```yaml
# coder-infra/docker-compose.local.yml

version: '3.8'

services:
  sudopod-api:
    # Mount source for hot reload (optional)
    volumes:
      - ./src:/app/src:ro
      - sudopod-credentials:/var/lib/sudopod
    environment:
      - NODE_ENV=development
      - SUDOPOD_API_KEYS=dev-api-key
      - LOG_LEVEL=debug

  coder:
    environment:
      # No OIDC in local dev - use password auth
      - CODER_OIDC_ISSUER_URL=
      - CODER_OIDC_CLIENT_ID=
      - CODER_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=
```

### Environment File

```bash
# coder-infra/.env.example

# === Local Development Defaults ===
SUDOPOD_API_KEYS=dev-api-key
CODER_ACCESS_URL=http://localhost:7080
CODER_ADMIN_EMAIL=admin@localhost

# === Ports (change if conflicts) ===
SUDOPOD_PORT=8080
CODER_PORT=7080

# === Optional: Pin Coder version ===
# CODER_VERSION=v2.8.0
```

## Dockerfile

```dockerfile
# coder-infra/Dockerfile

FROM node:20-alpine AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY tsconfig.json ./
COPY src ./src
RUN npm run build

FROM node:20-alpine
WORKDIR /app
RUN apk add --no-cache curl
COPY --from=builder /app/dist ./dist
COPY --from=builder /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY package*.json ./
RUN mkdir -p /var/lib/sudopod
USER node
EXPOSE 8080
CMD ["node", "dist/main.js"]
```

## Admin Bootstrap

The sudopod-api automatically bootstraps on first startup:

```typescript
// coder-infra/src/bootstrap.ts

const CREDENTIALS_PATH = '/var/lib/sudopod/coder-credentials.json';

export interface CoderCredentials {
  adminToken: string;
  adminEmail: string;
  adminUsername: string;
  bootstrappedAt: string;
}

export async function bootstrapCoder(coderUrl: string): Promise<CoderCredentials> {
  // Check if already bootstrapped
  if (fs.existsSync(CREDENTIALS_PATH)) {
    const credentials = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(CREDENTIALS_PATH, 'utf-8'));
    if (await validateToken(coderUrl, credentials.adminToken)) {
      return credentials;
    }
  }

  // Wait for Coder to be ready
  await waitForCoder(coderUrl);

  // Create first admin user (no auth required on fresh Coder)
  const adminEmail = process.env.CODER_ADMIN_EMAIL || 'admin@sudocode.local';
  const adminUsername = 'sudopod-admin';
  const adminPassword = crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex');

  await fetch(`${coderUrl}/api/v2/users/first`, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ email: adminEmail, username: adminUsername, password: adminPassword }),
  });

  // Login to get session token
  const loginRes = await fetch(`${coderUrl}/api/v2/users/login`, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ email: adminEmail, password: adminPassword }),
  });
  const sessionToken = (await loginRes.json()).session_token;

  // Create long-lived API token
  const tokenRes = await fetch(`${coderUrl}/api/v2/users/me/keys`, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Coder-Session-Token': sessionToken, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ lifetime: 0 }), // ~100 year default
  });
  const { key: adminToken } = await tokenRes.json();

  // Persist credentials
  const credentials: CoderCredentials = {
    adminToken,
    adminEmail,
    adminUsername,
    bootstrappedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
  };
  fs.writeFileSync(CREDENTIALS_PATH, JSON.stringify(credentials, null, 2), { mode: 0o600 });

  return credentials;
}
```

## Running Without Docker

For faster iteration during development:

```bash
# Terminal 1: Start Coder + Postgres only
docker compose up -d postgres coder

# Terminal 2: Run sudopod-api locally
npm install
npm run build
CODER_URL=http://localhost:7080 \
SUDOPOD_API_KEYS=dev-api-key \
npm start
```

## Testing

### Manual API Testing

```bash
# Health check
curl http://localhost:8080/health

# Create workspace
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/workspaces \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer dev-api-key" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "repository": "octocat/Hello-World",
    "userIdentity": {"email": "test@example.com"}
  }'

# List workspaces
curl http://localhost:8080/workspaces?owner=test \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer dev-api-key"

# Get workspace
curl http://localhost:8080/workspaces/WORKSPACE_ID \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer dev-api-key"

# Delete workspace
curl -X DELETE http://localhost:8080/workspaces/WORKSPACE_ID \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer dev-api-key"
```

### Integration Tests

```bash
# Run integration tests against local stack
npm run test:integration

# Or with docker compose
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.test.yml run --rm test
```

```typescript
// coder-infra/tests/integration/api.test.ts

import { describe, it, expect, beforeAll, afterAll } from 'vitest';

const API_URL = process.env.API_URL || 'http://localhost:8080';
const API_KEY = process.env.API_KEY || 'dev-api-key';

describe('CoderProvider API', () => {
  let workspaceId: string;

  it('health check returns ok', async () => {
    const res = await fetch(`${API_URL}/health`);
    expect(res.ok).toBe(true);
    const body = await res.json();
    expect(body.ok).toBe(true);
  });

  it('rejects requests without API key', async () => {
    const res = await fetch(`${API_URL}/workspaces`);
    expect(res.status).toBe(401);
  });

  it('creates a workspace', async () => {
    const res = await fetch(`${API_URL}/workspaces`, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: {
        'Authorization': `Bearer ${API_KEY}`,
        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({
        repository: 'octocat/Hello-World',
        userIdentity: { email: 'test@example.com' },
      }),
    });

    expect(res.status).toBe(201);
    const workspace = await res.json();
    expect(workspace.id).toBeDefined();
    expect(workspace.status).toMatch(/pending|starting/);
    
    workspaceId = workspace.id;
  });

  it('gets workspace by id', async () => {
    const res = await fetch(`${API_URL}/workspaces/${workspaceId}`, {
      headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${API_KEY}` },
    });

    expect(res.ok).toBe(true);
    const workspace = await res.json();
    expect(workspace.id).toBe(workspaceId);
  });

  it('deletes workspace', async () => {
    const res = await fetch(`${API_URL}/workspaces/${workspaceId}`, {
      method: 'DELETE',
      headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${API_KEY}` },
    });

    expect(res.status).toBe(204);
  });
});
```

content:
# Coder Provider Production Deployment

## Overview

This specification defines how to deploy the CoderProvider to production for use by sudocode-hub. It covers TLS termination, OIDC configuration, API key management, monitoring, backups, and operational procedures.

**Parent:** [[s-1u2m]] (Sudopod Provider Architecture)
**Local development:** [[s-7rdw]] (Coder Provider Local Development)
**Implements:** [[s-5lwn]] (CoderProvider Implementation)

## Goals

- Secure deployment with TLS and proper authentication
- OIDC integration (Google) for user browser login
- API key authentication for sudocode-hub
- Monitoring and alerting
- Backup and recovery procedures

## Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     Production Deployment                            │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                      │
│  Internet                                                            │
│      │                                                               │
│      ▼                                                               │
│  ┌──────────────────┐                                               │
│  │  Load Balancer   │  ◄── TLS termination                          │
│  │  (Cloud LB)      │      Let's Encrypt / ACM                      │
│  └──────────────────┘                                               │
│      │         │                                                     │
│      ▼         ▼                                                     │
│  ┌────────┐ ┌────────┐                                              │
│  │sudopod │ │ coder  │                                              │
│  │  :443  │ │  :443  │                                              │
│  └────────┘ └────────┘                                              │
│      │         │                                                     │
│      ▼         ▼                                                     │
│  ┌──────────────────┐         ┌──────────────────┐                  │
│  │   sudopod-api    │────────▶│     coder        │                  │
│  │   (internal)     │         │   (internal)     │                  │
│  └──────────────────┘         └──────────────────┘                  │
│           │                            │                             │
│           ▼                            ▼                             │
│  ┌──────────────────┐         ┌──────────────────┐                  │
│  │   credentials    │         │  Cloud SQL /     │                  │
│  │  (encrypted vol) │         │  RDS Postgres    │                  │
│  └──────────────────┘         └──────────────────┘                  │
│                                                                      │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Prerequisites

Before deploying:

1. **Domain names** registered and DNS configured:
   - `sudopod.yourdomain.com` - API endpoint
   - `coder.yourdomain.com` - Coder UI (for OIDC login)

2. **Google OAuth credentials** from Google Cloud Console:
   - Application type: Web application
   - Authorized redirect URI: `https://coder.yourdomain.com/api/v2/users/oidc/callback`

3. **Cloud infrastructure**:
   - Compute instance(s) with Docker
   - Managed PostgreSQL (Cloud SQL / RDS) or self-managed
   - Load balancer with TLS termination

## Docker Compose (Production)

```yaml
# coder-infra/docker-compose.prod.yml

version: '3.8'

services:
  # =========================================================================
  # Traefik: Reverse proxy with automatic TLS
  # =========================================================================
  traefik:
    image: traefik:v2.10
    command:
      - "--api.dashboard=false"
      - "--providers.docker=true"
      - "--providers.docker.exposedbydefault=false"
      - "--entrypoints.web.address=:80"
      - "--entrypoints.web.http.redirections.entryPoint.to=websecure"
      - "--entrypoints.websecure.address=:443"
      - "--certificatesresolvers.letsencrypt.acme.tlschallenge=true"
      - "--certificatesresolvers.letsencrypt.acme.email=${ACME_EMAIL}"
      - "--certificatesresolvers.letsencrypt.acme.storage=/letsencrypt/acme.json"
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
      - letsencrypt:/letsencrypt
    restart: unless-stopped

  # =========================================================================
  # sudopod-api: HTTP wrapper for CoderProvider
  # =========================================================================
  sudopod-api:
    image: ${SUDOPOD_IMAGE:-ghcr.io/sudocodeai/sudopod-api:latest}
    environment:
      - CODER_URL=http://coder:7080
      - CODER_TEMPLATE=${CODER_TEMPLATE:-sudocode-workspace}
      - SUDOPOD_API_KEYS=${SUDOPOD_API_KEYS}
      - CODER_ADMIN_EMAIL=${CODER_ADMIN_EMAIL}
      - NODE_ENV=production
    volumes:
      - sudopod-credentials:/var/lib/sudopod
    depends_on:
      coder:
        condition: service_healthy
    labels:
      - "traefik.enable=true"
      - "traefik.http.routers.sudopod.rule=Host(`${SUDOPOD_DOMAIN}`)"
      - "traefik.http.routers.sudopod.entrypoints=websecure"
      - "traefik.http.routers.sudopod.tls.certresolver=letsencrypt"
      - "traefik.http.services.sudopod.loadbalancer.server.port=8080"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:8080/health"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: '1'
          memory: 512M

  # =========================================================================
  # coder: Coder server (workspace orchestration)
  # =========================================================================
  coder:
    image: ghcr.io/coder/coder:${CODER_VERSION:-latest}
    environment:
      # Core config
      - CODER_ACCESS_URL=https://${CODER_DOMAIN}
      - CODER_HTTP_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0:7080
      - CODER_PG_CONNECTION_URL=${DATABASE_URL}
      
      # OIDC Configuration (Google)
      - CODER_OIDC_ISSUER_URL=https://accounts.google.com
      - CODER_OIDC_CLIENT_ID=${OIDC_CLIENT_ID}
      - CODER_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=${OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET}
      - CODER_OIDC_EMAIL_DOMAIN=${OIDC_EMAIL_DOMAIN:-*}
      - CODER_OIDC_ALLOW_SIGNUPS=true
      - CODER_OIDC_SIGN_IN_TEXT=Sign in with Google
      - CODER_OIDC_ICON_URL=/icon/google.svg
      
      # Security
      - CODER_TELEMETRY_ENABLE=false
      - CODER_SECURE_AUTH_COOKIE=true
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - coder-data:/var/lib/coder
    labels:
      - "traefik.enable=true"
      - "traefik.http.routers.coder.rule=Host(`${CODER_DOMAIN}`)"
      - "traefik.http.routers.coder.entrypoints=websecure"
      - "traefik.http.routers.coder.tls.certresolver=letsencrypt"
      - "traefik.http.services.coder.loadbalancer.server.port=7080"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:7080/api/v2/buildinfo"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 120s
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: '2'
          memory: 2G

volumes:
  letsencrypt:
  sudopod-credentials:
  coder-data:

networks:
  default:
    name: coder-network
```

## Environment Configuration

```bash
# coder-infra/.env.prod

# === Domains ===
SUDOPOD_DOMAIN=sudopod.yourdomain.com
CODER_DOMAIN=coder.yourdomain.com
ACME_EMAIL=admin@yourdomain.com

# === API Keys (generate with: openssl rand -hex 32) ===
# Multiple keys supported, comma-separated
SUDOPOD_API_KEYS=key1_for_hub,key2_for_backup

# === Database (use managed PostgreSQL in production) ===
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://coder:PASSWORD@db.example.com:5432/coder?sslmode=require

# === OIDC (Google) ===
OIDC_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id.apps.googleusercontent.com
OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret
OIDC_EMAIL_DOMAIN=*  # or restrict to your domain

# === Bootstrap ===
CODER_ADMIN_EMAIL=admin@yourdomain.com

# === Versions (pin for stability) ===
CODER_VERSION=v2.8.0
SUDOPOD_IMAGE=ghcr.io/sudocodeai/sudopod-api:v1.0.0
```

## Deployment Steps

### 1. Provision Infrastructure

```bash
# Example: GCP
gcloud compute instances create coder-provider \
  --machine-type=e2-standard-4 \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2204-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --tags=http-server,https-server

# Create managed PostgreSQL
gcloud sql instances create coder-db \
  --database-version=POSTGRES_15 \
  --tier=db-custom-2-4096 \
  --region=us-central1
```

### 2. Configure DNS

Point your domains to the instance IP:
```
sudopod.yourdomain.com  A  <instance-ip>
coder.yourdomain.com    A  <instance-ip>
```

### 3. Setup Server

```bash
# SSH to instance
gcloud compute ssh coder-provider

# Install Docker
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh
sudo usermod -aG docker $USER

# Clone repo
git clone https://github.com/sudocodeai/coder-infra
cd coder-infra

# Configure environment
cp .env.prod.example .env.prod
vim .env.prod  # Fill in values
```

### 4. Deploy

```bash
# Start services
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file .env.prod up -d

# Watch logs
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml logs -f

# Verify
curl https://sudopod.yourdomain.com/health
```

### 5. Push Template

```bash
# Login to Coder (creates admin user on first run)
coder login https://coder.yourdomain.com

# Push workspace template
cd templates/sudocode-workspace
coder templates push sudocode-workspace --yes
```

### 6. Test E2E Flow

```bash
# 1. Create workspace via API
curl -X POST https://sudopod.yourdomain.com/workspaces \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "repository": "octocat/Hello-World",
    "userIdentity": {"email": "your-email@gmail.com"}
  }'

# 2. Open browser: https://coder.yourdomain.com
# 3. Click "Sign in with Google"
# 4. Login with same email
# 5. Verify workspace appears in dashboard
```

## API Key Management

### Generate Keys

```bash
# Generate a new API key
openssl rand -hex 32

# Or use a password manager
```

### Rotate Keys

```bash
# 1. Add new key to .env.prod (comma-separated)
SUDOPOD_API_KEYS=old_key,new_key

# 2. Restart sudopod-api
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml restart sudopod-api

# 3. Update clients (sudocode-hub) to use new key

# 4. Remove old key
SUDOPOD_API_KEYS=new_key

# 5. Restart again
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml restart sudopod-api
```

### Key Security

- Store keys in secret manager (GCP Secret Manager, AWS Secrets Manager)
- Never commit keys to git
- Rotate keys periodically (quarterly)
- Use different keys for different clients

## Monitoring

### Prometheus Metrics

The sudopod-api exposes metrics at `/metrics`:

```yaml
# Add to docker-compose.prod.yml

  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus:latest
    volumes:
      - ./prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml
      - prometheus-data:/prometheus
    command:
      - '--config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml'
    restart: unless-stopped

  grafana:
    image: grafana/grafana:latest
    environment:
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${GRAFANA_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - grafana-data:/var/lib/grafana
    labels:
      - "traefik.enable=true"
      - "traefik.http.routers.grafana.rule=Host(`grafana.${DOMAIN}`)"
      - "traefik.http.routers.grafana.tls.certresolver=letsencrypt"
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  prometheus-data:
  grafana-data:
```

```yaml
# prometheus.yml
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: 'sudopod-api'
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['sudopod-api:8080']
    metrics_path: /metrics

  - job_name: 'coder'
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['coder:2112']
```

### Key Metrics

| Metric | Description | Alert Threshold |
|--------|-------------|-----------------|
| `sudopod_workspaces_created_total` | Total workspaces created | N/A (track rate) |
| `sudopod_request_duration_seconds` | Request latency | p99 > 5s |
| `sudopod_errors_total` | Error count by type | > 10/min |
| `up{job="sudopod-api"}` | Service health | == 0 |

### Health Checks

```bash
# sudopod-api health
curl https://sudopod.yourdomain.com/health

# Coder health
curl https://coder.yourdomain.com/api/v2/buildinfo
```

## Backups

### What to Backup

| Data | Location | Frequency | Retention |
|------|----------|-----------|-----------|
| PostgreSQL | Cloud SQL / RDS | Automated daily | 30 days |
| Admin credentials | sudopod-credentials volume | After bootstrap | Indefinite |
| Coder state | coder-data volume | Daily | 7 days |
| TLS certificates | letsencrypt volume | After renewal | N/A |

### Manual Backup

```bash
# Backup credentials volume
docker run --rm \
  -v sudopod-credentials:/data \
  -v $(pwd)/backups:/backup \
  alpine tar czf /backup/credentials-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz /data

# Backup coder data
docker run --rm \
  -v coder-data:/data \
  -v $(pwd)/backups:/backup \
  alpine tar czf /backup/coder-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz /data
```

### Restore

```bash
# Restore credentials
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml down
docker run --rm \
  -v sudopod-credentials:/data \
  -v $(pwd)/backups:/backup \
  alpine sh -c "rm -rf /data/* && tar xzf /backup/credentials-YYYYMMDD.tar.gz -C /"
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d
```

## Disaster Recovery

### Scenario: Complete Data Loss

1. Provision new infrastructure
2. Deploy docker-compose
3. Restore PostgreSQL from backup
4. Restore credentials volume from backup
5. Verify services healthy
6. Re-push template if needed

### Scenario: API Key Compromised

1. Immediately rotate key (see API Key Management)
2. Review logs for unauthorized access
3. Invalidate any sessions/workspaces created by attacker

### Scenario: OIDC Credentials Compromised

1. Revoke credentials in Google Cloud Console
2. Create new OAuth credentials
3. Update .env.prod with new credentials
4. Restart Coder

## Security Checklist

- [ ] TLS enabled for all endpoints
- [ ] OIDC configured with production credentials
- [ ] API keys are strong (32+ bytes)
- [ ] API keys stored in secret manager
- [ ] Database uses SSL connection
- [ ] Docker socket access limited
- [ ] Firewall rules restrict access
- [ ] Health endpoints don't require auth (for load balancer)
- [ ] Logs don't contain secrets
- [ ] Backup encryption enabled

## Operational Procedures

### Deploy New Version

```bash
# Pull new image
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml pull

# Rolling restart
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d --no-deps sudopod-api

# Verify health
curl https://sudopod.yourdomain.com/health
```

### View Logs

```bash
# All services
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml logs -f

# Specific service
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml logs -f sudopod-api

# Search for errors
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml logs sudopod-api 2>&1 | grep -i error
```

### Debug Connectivity

```bash
# Check internal connectivity
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml exec sudopod-api \
  wget -q -O- http://coder:7080/api/v2/buildinfo

# Check external connectivity
curl -v https://sudopod.yourdomain.com/health
```
